subject: TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD function
notes: CLOSED BY kb/Work PB248. cite.py --check 15.91.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer." => OK (15.91.3 1); the integer TYPE it invokes is 15.3 type 6, --check OK. THE ROW'S TEST-REF WAS DELIBERATELY EMPTY - the refuter recorded that no fixture wrote a bad argument to THIS function and that IntrinsicArgumentClassDriftTests only asserted a row EXISTS, never what it rejects. That is the gap the new drift test closes structurally rather than by adding a fixture per function: EveryIntegerArgumentPosition_RejectsAFloatingPointItem walks IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified, collects EVERY position (and tail position) whose Kind is 'i' - TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD's included, by name - and asserts Violation() returns non-null for a floating-point item at each, once per floating-point Usage member. The unswept sibling arm the row named (a COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-* item is Category numeric with Scale 0, so the `Scale: > 0` guard never fired) is gone: PicInfo.IsIntegerDescription now carries 15.3 type 6's requirement in one place and both integer screens read it. The E-form LITERAL sibling and the additive-EXPRESSION sibling were closed in the same change set. Proven not-blind: the drift test was run against the pre-fix predicate and failed on all ten float usages.
